study_identification_part.si4_title: Heterogeneity of morphometric similarity networks in health and schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply longitudinal normative modeling to regional morphometric similarity to quantify individual deviations and their changes over time in schizophrenia versus healthy controls, and assess group differences at baseline and follow-up.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Welch t-tests for group comparisons of network-averaged z-scores (FDR-corrected); two-proportions z-tests for infra/supra-normal proportions per region; Pearson correlations in SZ between baseline z-scores/change in outlier count and IQ and PANSS total/positive/negative/general scores; GAMs to residualize raw MS (age smooth, sex, Euler, scanner) before diagnostic t-tests.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: At baseline, SZ showed reduced morphometric similarity in the default mode network and increased in somatomotor; the proportion of individuals with infra/supra-normal deviations per region was low (<6%) in both groups; longitudinal within-person changes in outlier counts were minimal (<1) and not different between groups; normative modeling improved group-level sensitivity versus raw MS.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Baseline network-level differences: DMN t = -3.665, PFDR < 0.05; Somatomotor t = 2.940, PFDR < 0.05 (Table 1B; Supplemental Table A). Follow-up DMN t = -2.046 (uncorrected p = 0.041). The percentage of test-set individuals with |z|>1.96 per region was <6% for both HC and SZ at both timepoints. Mean within-group change in total outlier regions over time was <1 in both groups, with no significant between-group difference. Supplemental analyses indicated increased statistical significance using normative model z-scores compared to residualized raw MS.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Mapped DKT regions to Yeo-7 functional networks; replicated global MS maps (r≈0.8) with prior work; included Euler number to mitigate image quality variance; evaluated on held-out test sets with EV, MSLL, skewness, kurtosis; used z-diff for longitudinal change.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Explained variance differed among regions, with some regions showing low variance, suggesting age-dependency varies by region; deviations showed limited associations with symptom severity and cognition; morphometric similarity's utility in SZ may be nuanced.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Train/test splits preserved age/sex/scanner distributions per dataset (caret::createDataPartition). For the clinical dataset, all SZ and 80% HCs were in test; remaining 20% HCs contributed to training. Baseline and follow-up scans were acquired on the same scanner for each participant; two identical scanners were used in the clinical cohort.
